graph.title: Enforce campaign ownership across all campaign actions and resources
graph.body:
<!-- roadmap-slicer:edda-story-led-srd-521:issue:ownership -->
A signed-in user can read or delete a campaign owned by another user when given its campaign ID. The same missing ownership boundary affects campaign-scoped resources and actions.

Epic: #48 Make campaign actions private, durable and recoverable
Roadmap: #47 [Roadmap] Story-led Edda gameplay with SRD 5.2.1

**Delivery unit: one PR** (size L). Implement this outcome with its tests and docs. Do not absorb neighbouring issues; if it grows past one reviewable PR, split it and update the roadmap. Needs a human checkpoint: Security boundary changes need a human review before merge.

## Blocked by

Nothing; this can start now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Foreign-account requests are denied without disclosing or changing campaign data.
- [ ] Owner requests continue to work; nested resources remain scoped to their campaign.
- [ ] Regression coverage uses two distinct users and includes live-connection access.

## Verification

- `go test -short -race ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- For database changes, run `go test -tags integration -run Integration ./internal/handlers ./internal/state/sqlc` against isolated PostgreSQL.

## Code boundaries

- internal/engine
- internal/game
- internal/domain
- pkg/api
- queries
- migrations

These are starting points, not a list of files to edit.

## Out of scope

- Production deployment, destructive data conversion and unrelated cleanup.

## Notes

Use deterministic model doubles and injectable dice; no production accounts or paid inference are needed for mechanical checks. Preserve legacy campaign reads and the shared web/TUI engine boundary. One issue closes with one reviewable PR; do not absorb neighboring roadmap work.

Original review evidence and reproduction details are retained below. Source review was at b84d5dc; recheck current behavior before changing it.

<details>
<summary>Original review evidence and reproduction record</summary>

## What happened

A signed-in user can read or delete a campaign owned by another user when given its campaign ID. The same missing ownership boundary affects campaign-scoped resources and actions.

## What I expected

Only the campaign owner can access its data or change its state, including through a live connection.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create two test accounts and a campaign owned by account A.
2. Authenticate as account B and request account A's campaign by ID, then attempt a campaign deletion in a disposable fixture.
3. Check other campaign resources, exports, saves, journal, turn submission and live-connection access.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Foreign-account requests are denied without disclosing or changing campaign data.
- [ ] Owner requests continue to work; nested resources remain scoped to their campaign.
- [ ] Regression coverage uses two distinct users and includes live-connection access.

## Evidence and limits

Reproduced locally through the real router and JWT middleware with an in-memory campaign/query fixture: foreign GET returned 200; DELETE reached the deletion stub and returned 204. No production data was accessed or deleted.

## Review context

Found during the backend-first repository mapping/review on 2026-11-14 at commit [b84d5dc](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/commit/b84d5dc8bde8438920c867c2dab4d64c50c001b5).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Original review evidence and reproduction record</summary>

## What happened

Two overlapping turns for the same campaign can both succeed with the same turn number. Both requests can act on the same earlier campaign history.

## What I expected

A campaign's turns have a deterministic order and unique turn numbers, including when multiple tabs or clients submit actions.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a disposable campaign and a controllable model stub.
2. Start two turn requests for that campaign; pause model responses until both requests have loaded history.
3. Release both responses and inspect the saved turn numbers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Concurrent same-campaign requests are ordered or explicitly rejected without duplicate turn numbers.
- [ ] The database protects the campaign/turn-number invariant.
- [ ] Independent campaigns can still process turns concurrently.

## Evidence and limits

Reproduced with a race-enabled local probe using a barrier-controlled model stub and a synchronized state store: both successful requests saved turn 1. This is a logical concurrency defect; the normal race suite passed.

## Review context

<details>
<summary>Original review evidence and reproduction record</summary>

## What happened

A turn can change campaign state and then return an error when saving its session history. Those changes remain even though the player receives a failed turn.

## What I expected

Turn results, durable campaign changes and history agree. A failed or retried request must not silently apply the same effect twice.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a disposable campaign and a model stub that requests a visible campaign-state change.
2. Allow that change to succeed, then inject a failure while saving the turn history.
3. Inspect campaign state and history, then retry the action.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Define and enforce a durable turn-completion boundary with explicit recovery behavior.
- [ ] Failure after a state change cannot leave an untracked successful effect.
- [ ] Regression coverage exercises failed completion and safe retry without duplicated effects.

## Evidence and limits

Reproduced locally with a mutating test tool and an injected history-save error: the turn returned an error while the mutation remained. Repeated effects on retries are a risk to test, not a demonstrated production outcome.

## Review context

Found during the backend-first repository mapping/review on 2026-11-14 at commit [b84d5dc](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/commit/b84d5dc8bde8438920c867c2dab4d64c50c001b5).

</details>

This PR establishes the atomic mechanical commit/history boundary. Durable narration retries are a separate issue. Do not hold a database transaction through a model call.

graph.title: Investigate turn-stream cleanup when the live client disconnects
graph.body:
<!-- roadmap-slicer:edda-story-led-srd-521:issue:stream-cancel -->
Turn events are sent through a bounded channel. A failed live-connection write cancels the turn and stops consuming events; event publication does not consistently observe cancellation.

Epic: #48 Make campaign actions private, durable and recoverable
Roadmap: #47 [Roadmap] Story-led Edda gameplay with SRD 5.2.1

**Spike, time-boxed to one working session; record reproduction, counterevidence and a bounded fix if needed.** The deliverable is a decision, not production code. Record the answer as a comment, update any dependent issue it changes, then close this issue so the work it blocks can start. An agent can finish this alone.

## Question

Disconnecting a client cannot leave a turn worker blocked while publishing status or completion events. Establish a reproduction or counterevidence before proposing a fix.

## Blocked by

- #45 Add behavior regression coverage before the frontend overhaul

## Out of scope

## Remaining execution plan — November 16 UTC / November 15 Chicago

[Complete roadmap and development plan](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/4ae44d2f4d0b5216c474211d9010d17920b179c6/docs/remaining-development-plan.md) · [All-issue dependency snapshot](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/4ae44d2f4d0b5216c474211d9010d17920b179c6/docs/remaining-issues.json) · Documentation PR #345.

The refreshed snapshot has **200 open issues: 11 tracking issues and 189 work issues**. Every remaining issue is listed once in the plan, with its native parent, open blockers, dependency wave and verification requirements. This section is the current execution guidance; the original waves below retain delivery history.

1. **Qualify the current playable slice (3 issues): #46 → #78 → #89.** Record the visible phone-keyboard and human/accessibility evidence, reuse the qualification work in #343, and retain the declared partial-coverage boundary. #342 is closed through #344; its exact Athletics request prepares a preview and does not enable general SRD free text.
2. **Safe contracts and useful gameplay (19 issues):** start #143, #194, #195 and #284 alongside the qualification lane. Then prefer the bounded #338/#339 Fighter actions, #148 Bandit, #263 → #266 ally healing, and #145 → #264 light. The plan enumerates all 15 runtime slices and their exact prerequisites.
3. **Source catalogues (132 data PRs):** #151–#178/#184 monsters, #196–#224 spells, #225–#262 items/equipment and #285–#320 characters. Each follows its own contract; data alone cannot enable playable support.

Deliver readable story-led play, an interactive rules-backed character sheet, grounded action assistance and faithful chapters across desktop and phone, while keeping the main gameplay screen within one viewport like the current app.

## How to use this roadmap

This roadmap and its epics are tracking issues, not implementation PRs. Each work issue is **one reviewable PR**, and native GitHub dependencies set the order: an issue is ready when every issue it depends on is closed. Close a work issue from its merged PR with `Closes #<n>`. Tracking issues depend on their children, so they close last.

Plan: [Detailed product and implementation plan](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/c2beafa55ff18b8d880096dcba56914a6870ed29/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-14-story-led-rules-gameplay.md), source commit `c2beafa`. The plan defines the complete target; work below is split into reviewable PRs and bounded investigations.

## Decisions

- SRD 5.2.1 is the pinned rules reference; use one authoritative server rules/action path.
- Story-led play; interactive sheet with targets/options/costs; rolls happen on confirmation with inspectable results.
- Narrative combat with initiative, explicit range/conditions and target selection; no required grid UI.
- Main gameplay fits one viewport on desktop and phone, with internal transcript/detail scrolling and anchored reachable action controls.
- Preserve the current Art Deco design language and the overall choice-based campaign creation process.
- Ghost text accepts with Tab or touch into an editable draft; accepting a suggestion never submits it.
- Faithful chapters follow played outcomes without invented events or hidden lore.

## Shared delivery rules

- Every work issue is one reviewable PR; spikes finish with a recorded decision and bounded follow-up issues.
- Reuse review issues #28-#46; evidence and original acceptance criteria are retained. No automation/agent queue labels are applied.
- Preserve legacy modes, data, public routes and the shared web/TUI boundary; new rules support is versioned and explicitly partial until qualified.
- Viewport contract: no document overflow at the specified default desktop/tablet/phone sizes; long content scrolls internally; keyboard-open and accessibility reflow require separate checks.
- Full coverage remains an epic exit criterion. Character/spell/world expansion spikes publish exact follow-up PRs into this roadmap and extend native dependencies; initial batches are not the whole SRD.
- No implementation, deployment, destructive conversion or production data mutation is authorized by publication.
- Size L warnings are retained only for a named integration boundary or fixture. They are review-size estimates, not delivery dates; split and update the graph if evidence exceeds that boundary.
- The final campaign qualification joins independent completed capabilities, so its real prerequisite fan-in exceeds five. Transitive prerequisite edges are removed; no artificial serial chain was introduced to hide this warning.

## Out of scope

- A tactical grid editor, new brand, cooperative multiplayer, non-SRD commercial catalogue, marketplace, native app and unrelated infrastructure changes.

## Wave 14 independent qualification

[Candidate evidence](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/d103c0b/docs/playtest/issue-89/README.md) is in draft PR #343. Local evidence passes: 64 frontend unit tests, 93 Chromium browser cases with one worker and unchanged timeouts/assertions, build, focused changed-file lint, full Go short race/vet, disposable PostgreSQL handler/state suites and TUI fixtures. Whole-tree frontend lint retains 22 baseline errors. These are separate component/contract fixtures, not a single continuous real-browser/real-database campaign or a production deployment.

The candidate fixes explicit same-action recovery after a server error, with campaign ID isolation and optimistic-entry/history reconciliation. It intentionally leaves #89 open: the fresh Android attempt again hit DEVICE_IN_USE owned by another session, and a final human player-experience review is not recorded. #46/#78 remain open.

Real PostgreSQL evidence also exposes the SRD free-text gap: typed actions succeed, but ordinary text reaches the intentional legacy guard. #342 is a bounded implementation under #50, with prerequisites #64/#88, Size L, and a native blocker of #89. It prepares only `Make an Athletics check` through the authoritative preview/explicit-confirm path; arbitrary text and legacy mutations stay unavailable. Independent implementation is proceeding in a separate PR; no unsupported pass is claimed here.

graph.title: Define turn lifetime when a live client disconnects during silent model work
graph.body:
Follow-up from the #37 spike; roadmap #47 / epic #48. One focused PR after a lifetime decision, coordinated with #59 recovery.

The handler only reads between turns. A disconnected peer is observed on the next write, so a silent provider call can continue until it returns or the turn timeout expires. Cancellation-aware publication fixes blocked sends, but cannot stop a dependency that ignores context or define whether already committed work should continue.

Acceptance:
- Choose and document the turn ownership contract during disconnect (including committed effects and reconnect recovery).
- Add a deterministic silent model/tool fixture and distinguish disconnect detection, context cancellation, provider exit and worker exit with bounded deadlines.
- Implement the selected handler lifetime/read or heartbeat strategy without concurrent websocket readers or duplicate turns.
- Preserve #59 committed-result recovery and test timeout plus reconnect behavior.

Excludes provider redesign, frontend layout, deployment, rollback of committed mutations and paid/live inference.

graph.title: Release consumed live events with a sequence-based acknowledgment cursor
graph.body:
Follow-up from #43 spike, roadmap #47 / epic #48. One focused PR. Preserve the #42 campaign identity boundary.

Replace the lifetime append-only transport array/count cursor with consumption acknowledgments or a sequence-based bounded queue. Do not slice the existing array: narrativeReducer.processedEventCount is an array index and would then skip or replay frames.

Acceptance:
- Release every processed transport batch after narrative reduction; use monotonic event sequence/acknowledgment semantics so batched bursts lose no results or errors.
- Define a maximum pending queue or backpressure/recovery policy for a suspended consumer; justify the bound from the deterministic #43 baseline.
- Preserve all durable transcript entries; status updates need only the latest display state. Do not truncate durable history to satisfy transport memory checks.
- Re-run the #43 long-session probe and assert retained transport payload is independent of completed turn count.
- Cover more frames than the bound in one batch, campaign changes, same-campaign reconnect, history loading versus live completion, chunk/result/error ordering and unmount cleanup. Durable replay/deduplication must be explicit if protocol IDs change.

Excludes transcript virtualization (#90), model token streaming (#41), chapter generation, production profiling and deployment. The existing retention probe intentionally characterizes the baseline; convert it to bounded assertions with this implementation.

graph.body:
<!-- edda-271:effect-identity -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 162, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

Two explicitly prepared level-one Clerics cast Shield of Faith at separate times on one known creature within 60 feet, then one caster ends concentration.

## Targets

One known same-campaign creature per cast; retain the existing conscious-self path. Require authoritative range and clear path; reject unknown range, total cover, foreign or hidden recipients.

## Costs

Each cast: one level-one slot, Bonus Action, V/S and noncostly material/focus availability; one-slot-per-turn limit. Voluntary ending: no action or slot refund.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Absolute start/expiry seconds, maximum 600 seconds. Replace only the casting caster’s previous concentration. Equal-potency overlapping +2 AC applies once, latest casting active; ending it reveals an older still-live effect without restarting its clock.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `effect.instance.caster-recipient`, `effect.same-spell.latest-equal`, `effect.duration.absolute`, `concentration.owner`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Persist cast identity separately from recipient links; remove all links only for the ended cast. Different casters never overwrite each other. Preserve old self-only saves and unrelated stats.

- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. graph.title: Enforce Rage casting and Concentration restrictions
graph.body:
<!-- edda-321:rage-casting -->
Parent: #283; decision #321; roadmap #47; blocks #498; #498 directly blocks #337.

Delivery: one reviewable PR, Task Size M.

Source: pinned English SRD5.2.1 pp28-30 and explicitly named referenced pages below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md.

Scope and deterministic positive fixture: PDF p29: Rage cannot maintain Concentration and cannot cast spells, including other-class, feat, ritual, scroll/item spell routes. One authoritative cast validation boundary with #273; end existing Concentration via #353 lifecycle on Rage entry, never a second effect store. Nonspell item actions retain own rules. Block both forged direct calls and client discovery.

Negative fixtures: violate each stated eligibility/number/target/action/resource/timing predicate independently; reject unsupported variants and forged levels. Preview and cancellation never mutate.

Required acceptance: Authoritative campaign/actor/source/rules-version/class-level eligibility; isolated high-level test entitlements grant no production access. Prepare previews costs/choices/targets/timing without dice or writes; explicit confirm revalidates current revision and commits choices, injectable dice, resource/action costs, effects, derived sheet and public history atomically. Store durable action receipt: same-ID retry/reload/reconnect returns exact committed result with no reroll/recharge/regrant; conflicting payload or concurrent stale confirmation rejected; two concurrent confirmations spend/apply once. Inject history/effect/choice failure and prove full PostgreSQL rollback. Protect private NPC HP, hidden actors, tactics and private choices in discovery/preview/history/error/reconnect. Shared web/TUI availability, disabled reason, accessible confirmation/cancel and reconnect fixtures required; desktop/phone confirmation journeys for changed web UI. Unknown prerequisites fail closed. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL integration rollback/replay/reload/concurrency tests; frontend build, changed-file lint and behavior fixtures when UI changes. Preserve legacy reads/unrelated JSON; retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptations. No production deployment, inference or broad coverage promotion.

Ownership: feature resolvers own behavior; level/entry applications consume them and apply grants once. Feature tests use explicit isolated entitlements, never grant production class admission. Data and earlier levels never unlock broader support. Shared #272 rests, #273 casting, #333 origins, #335 multiclass, #336 advancement, #384 selection/#389 ability updater, #269/#270 conditions and #278 equipment retain their scopes. Exact shared terminals in this matrix must block #498 natively; #498 blocks #337. Planning closure is insufficient. Selected feat effect must have its own terminal gate before admission; never implement spell/item effects here. No child implementation or qualification is supplied by this decision.

Native blocked-by: #273, #286, #308, #351, #353, #434.

Scope: PDF31: primaryCHA,d8,DEX/CHA saves,any3 distinct skills,Simple weapons,any3 Musical Instruments,Light armor. Choose A Leather Armor+2 Daggers+chosen instrument+Entertainer pack+19GP OR B90GP. Package instrument separate from three proficiency choices. Consume #430 provenance and #195/#278 item identities; no background/species effects. Unknown item behavior stays unavailable.

Negative deterministic fixture: Reject duplicate/unknown selections,A+B,extra saves,forged items; origin duplicate replacement requires explicit source rule.

Parent: #501; decision #322; roadmap #47. Task Size M.

One reviewable PR. Required path: this terminal -> Bard gate #501 -> #337. Additional direct qualification gates: [].

Source: pinned English SRD5.2.1 PDF31-35; exact referenced pages in scope below. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. Attribution/license/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; CC-BY-4.0. Source facts paraphrased; fixture/ownership choices are Edda additions.

Scope: PDF31:9 exact slot columns at every Bard level,absent=0;spent ledgers survive advancement/reload,capacity changes invent no rest. Single-class table distinct from #335 combined slots. Long Rest #428 recovers;Short Rest #427 does not.

Positive deterministic fixture: Bard3 slots4/2;Bard18 slots4/3/3/3/3/1/1/1/1.

Negative deterministic fixture: Reject Short Rest restoration,absent slot,rest on level gain,mixed-class Bard-only table.

Required acceptance: For this one PR, preview is inert; explicit confirmation revalidates authoritative eligibility, source/version, target facts and expected revision. Persist choice, exact dice, once-only cost/use and history atomically. Receipt replay/retry/reload returns the same result without rerolling or charging again. Inject history failure for full rollback; race two confirmations and require one commit; stale/foreign/unsupported state rejects without mutation. Prove this with deterministic dice and isolated PostgreSQL handler/state fixtures. Disclose only player-known targets, choices, costs and source derivations; hidden/foreign facts never enter previews, receipts or errors. Shared engine serves web and TUI: explicitly expose supported choices or show unavailable with a reason on both; require desktop/phone confirmation and reconnect plus TUI behavior fixtures before availability. No Full Rules/coverage promotion. Higher-level isolated fixture state never grants production entitlement. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p 2 ./...; changed UI requires build, focused lint and behavior tests.

Feature tests use explicit isolated entitlements, never production grants. Transitions consume exact implemented contracts and apply grants once. Unknown options/effects/origins/multiclass configurations fail closed. #272/#427/#428 own completed rests; #273 casting modes, #58 sheet projection, #333/#430 proficiency provenance, #336/#429 advancement transaction, #335 multiclass contracts, #384 selection/#389 caps. #277 spells/#278 items/#269/#270 conditions retain shared effects. Chosen feat/spell effects require their exact terminal and qualification path before availability; source import or planning closure never supplies execution. No runtime/grants/coverage promotion or deployment in this decision.

<!-- edda-323:asi -->
Parent: #551; decision #323; roadmap #47. Task Size M.

Scope and deterministic positive acceptance: PDF37/87-88: one eligible feat grant at each4/8/12/16; ASI or other eligible feat, use #384 selector/#389 ability caps, exact chosen effect #385-401 before availability. Unique per-level grant receipt, not four implementations.

Negative acceptance: independently violate every stated level, option, source, timing, number, target and resource predicate; reject unsupported variants and forged entitlement without mutation.

Required acceptance: Authoritative campaign/actor/source/rules-version/class-level eligibility; isolated high-level test entitlements grant no production access. Prepare previews costs/choices/targets/timing without dice or writes; explicit confirm revalidates current revision and commits choices, injectable dice, resource/action costs, effects, derived sheet and public history atomically. Store durable action receipt: same-ID retry/reload/reconnect returns exact committed result with no reroll/recharge/regrant; conflicting payload or concurrent stale confirmation rejected; two concurrent confirmations spend/apply once. Inject history/effect/choice failure and prove full PostgreSQL rollback. Protect private NPC HP, hidden actors, tactics and private choices in discovery/preview/history/error/reconnect. Shared web/TUI availability, disabled reason, accessible confirmation/cancel and reconnect fixtures required; desktop/phone confirmation journeys for changed web UI. Unknown prerequisites fail closed. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL integration rollback/replay/reload/concurrency tests; frontend build, changed-file lint and behavior fixtures when UI changes. Preserve legacy reads/unrelated JSON; retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptations. No production deployment, inference or broad coverage promotion.

Feature resolvers own behavior with isolated test entitlements; transitions consume those contracts and apply grants once. #427/#428 own completed rests; #429 owns reusable XP/PB/CON transaction; #430 provenance; #503 list membership (not execution); #487/#488 conditions; #384-401 feat selection and effects. #502 remains Bard-specific. #279/#280 qualify spell/item effects; #181/#185 and #183 retain spell-created world lifecycle ownership. Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

Level 4 Transmutation (Bard, Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 60 feet
Components: V, S, M (a caterpillar cocoon)
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour
You attempt to transform a creature that you can
see within range into a Beast. The target must suc-
ceed on a Wisdom saving throw or shape-shift into
a Beast form for the duration. That form can be any
Beast you choose that has a Challenge Rating equal
to or less than the target’s (or the target’s level if
it doesn’t have a Challenge Rating). The target’s
game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the
chosen Beast, but the target retains its alignment,
personality, creature type, Hit Points, and Hit Point
Dice. See the “Animals” section of “Monsters” for a
sample of Beast stat blocks.
The target gains a number of Temporary Hit
Points equal to the Hit Points of the Beast form.
These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain
when the spell ends. The spell ends early on the tar-
get if it has no Temporary Hit Points left.
The target is limited in the actions it can perform
by the anatomy of its new form, and it can’t speak or
cast spells.
The target’s gear melds into the new form. The
creature can’t use or otherwise benefit from any of
that equipment.

Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

by the anatomy of its new form, and it can’t speak or
cast spells.
The target’s gear melds into the new form. The
creature can’t use or otherwise benefit from any of
that equipment.

the fire.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF48,87–88. Fighter4,6,8,12,14,16: ASI OR another qualifying feat. #384 durable choice; #389 ASI +2 one or+1 two max20,repeatable. <!-- edda-325:level-3 -->
Parent #728; decision #325; roadmap #47. One PR. Task Size M.

Required native path: this terminal -> #728 -> #337.

Pinned SRD5.2.1 PDF47–49 and explicitly cited consumed rules. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md. Fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF47–49,22–25. Exact Fighter row 3 and all nested choices/resources below. Earned total-character XP threshold; admitted prior adjacent Fighter level only, never skip levels. Preserve existing bounded Fighter1->2 fixed/roll retain-Defense/mastery fixture; new options require their exact owners. Apply new feature contracts once; cumulative Champion features at/below class level; refresh Second Wind/mastery/Surge/Indomitable table capacities, not free recovery on level-up; explicit optional base Fighting Style replacement at each Fighter level. Class feature execution is independently owned. All inherited features remain gated. No unrestricted direct higher-level creation.

For each exact predicate below: deterministic positive and independently violated negative fixtures, unsupported/forged origin/level/owner rejection, inert prepare/cancel with no dice/state/history changes, explicit confirmed choice, stale revision rejection, stable action-ID replay after lost response and durable reload, concurrent confirmation applies once, atomic cost/dice/history/database rollback including injected write failures, no private DC/hidden target/lore disclosure. Shared engine through web AND trusted TUI: disabled/unavailable explanations, confirmation/cancel/reconnect/retry and keyboard/phone journeys. Injectable dice unit tests plus isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests; frontend build/changed-file lint/behavior fixtures and TUI command tests. GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./... . Feature tests use isolated entitlements; only separately qualified admission/transition may grant them. Unknown outcomes never imply success/failure. Outcome-dependent reactions such as Tactical Mind and Indomitable require a disclosed qualifying outcome. Heroic Inspiration remains available immediately after an owned known die even when the DC and outcome are undisclosed. No inference, deployment, grants, coverage or Full Rules promotion from planning. For passive/automatic source benefits, confirmation belongs to the triggering action or turn; never invent an optional activation or extra action cost.

Ownership: execution and admission are separate contracts. #427/#428 completed rests under272; #429 reusable XP/PB/CON under336 (Barbarian adapter remains D12/fixed7); Fighter D10/fixed6 separately owned here. #430 under333 provenance; #333 origins/#335 multiclass retain policy. #384 durable choices/#389 capped ability application; #385–401 exact feat effects; #487 Incapacitated/Unconscious, #488 Charmed/Frightened/Prone; #489–496 eight separate masteries under278; #58 sheet. #273 casting modes is not sheet ownership. #351–353 and #382 retain exact effect/concentration/Cleric eligibility paths; this Fighter decision grants none of their access. No generic spell implementation.

Exact native prerequisites: #58, #336, #731, #733, #734, #739, #747, #748, #749, #755.

<!-- edda-325:level-10 -->
Parent #728; decision #325; roadmap #47. One PR. Task Size M.

Required native path: this terminal -> #728 -> #337.

Pinned SRD5.2.1 PDF47–49 and explicitly cited consumed rules. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md. Fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF47–49,22–25. Exact Fighter row 10 and all nested choices/resources below. Earned total-character XP threshold; admitted prior adjacent Fighter level only, never skip levels. Preserve existing bounded Fighter1->2 fixed/roll retain-Defense/mastery fixture; new options require their exact owners. Apply new feature contracts once; cumulative Champion features at/below class level; refresh Second Wind/mastery/Surge/Indomitable table capacities, not free recovery on level-up; explicit optional base Fighting Style replacement at each Fighter level. Class feature execution is independently owned. All inherited features remain gated. No unrestricted direct higher-level creation.

For each exact predicate below: deterministic positive and independently violated negative fixtures, unsupported/forged origin/level/owner rejection, inert prepare/cancel with no dice/state/history changes, explicit confirmed choice, stale revision rejection, stable action-ID replay after lost response and durable reload, concurrent confirmation applies once, atomic cost/dice/history/database rollback including injected write failures, no private DC/hidden target/lore disclosure. Shared engine through web AND trusted TUI: disabled/unavailable explanations, confirmation/cancel/reconnect/retry and keyboard/phone journeys. Injectable dice unit tests plus isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests; frontend build/changed-file lint/behavior fixtures and TUI command tests. GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./... . Feature tests use isolated entitlements; only separately qualified admission/transition may grant them. Unknown outcomes never imply success/failure. Outcome-dependent reactions such as Tactical Mind and Indomitable require a disclosed qualifying outcome. Heroic Inspiration remains available immediately after an owned known die even when the DC and outcome are undisclosed. No inference, deployment, grants, coverage or Full Rules promotion from planning. For passive/automatic source benefits, confirmation belongs to the triggering action or turn; never invent an optional activation or extra action cost.

Ownership: execution and admission are separate contracts. #427/#428 completed rests under272; #429 reusable XP/PB/CON under336 (Barbarian adapter remains D12/fixed7); Fighter D10/fixed6 separately owned here. #430 under333 provenance; #333 origins/#335 multiclass retain policy. #384 durable choices/#389 capped ability application; #385–401 exact feat effects; #487 Incapacitated/Unconscious, #488 Charmed/Frightened/Prone; #489–496 eight separate masteries under278; #58 sheet. #273 casting modes is not sheet ownership. #351–353 and #382 retain exact effect/concentration/Cleric eligibility paths; this Fighter decision grants none of their access. No generic spell implementation.

graph.body:
<!-- edda-325:level-12 -->
Parent #728; decision #325; roadmap #47. One PR. Task Size M.

Required native path: this terminal -> #728 -> #337.

Pinned SRD5.2.1 PDF47–49 and explicitly cited consumed rules. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md. Fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF47–49,22–25. Exact Fighter row 12 and all nested choices/resources below. Earned total-character XP threshold; admitted prior adjacent Fighter level only, never skip levels. Preserve existing bounded Fighter1->2 fixed/roll retain-Defense/mastery fixture; new options require their exact owners. Apply new feature contracts once; cumulative Champion features at/below class level; refresh Second Wind/mastery/Surge/Indomitable table capacities, not free recovery on level-up; explicit optional base Fighting Style replacement at each Fighter level. Class feature execution is independently owned. All inherited features remain gated. No unrestricted direct higher-level creation.

For each exact predicate below: deterministic positive and independently violated negative fixtures, unsupported/forged origin/level/owner rejection, inert prepare/cancel with no dice/state/history changes, explicit confirmed choice, stale revision rejection, stable action-ID replay after lost response and durable reload, concurrent confirmation applies once, atomic cost/dice/history/database rollback including injected write failures, no private DC/hidden target/lore disclosure. Shared engine through web AND trusted TUI: disabled/unavailable explanations, confirmation/cancel/reconnect/retry and keyboard/phone journeys. Injectable dice unit tests plus isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests; frontend build/changed-file lint/behavior fixtures and TUI command tests. GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./... . Feature tests use isolated entitlements; only separately qualified admission/transition may grant them. Unknown outcomes never imply success/failure. Outcome-dependent reactions such as Tactical Mind and Indomitable require a disclosed qualifying outcome. Heroic Inspiration remains available immediately after an owned known die even when the DC and outcome are undisclosed. No inference, deployment, grants, coverage or Full Rules promotion from planning. For passive/automatic source benefits, confirmation belongs to the triggering action or turn; never invent an optional activation or extra action cost.

Ownership: execution and admission are separate contracts. #427/#428 completed rests under272; #429 reusable XP/PB/CON under336 (Barbarian adapter remains D12/fixed7); Fighter D10/fixed6 separately owned here. #430 under333 provenance; #333 origins/#335 multiclass retain policy. #384 durable choices/#389 capped ability application; #385–401 exact feat effects; #487 Incapacitated/Unconscious, #488 Charmed/Frightened/Prone; #489–496 eight separate masteries under278; #58 sheet. #273 casting modes is not sheet ownership. #351–353 and #382 retain exact effect/concentration/Cleric eligibility paths; this Fighter decision grants none of their access. No generic spell implementation.

Exact native prerequisites: #58, #336, #731, #733, #734, #740, #764.

<!-- edda-325:level-19 -->
Parent #728; decision #325; roadmap #47. One PR. Task Size M.

Required native path: this terminal -> #728 -> #337.

Pinned SRD5.2.1 PDF47–49 and explicitly cited consumed rules. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md. Fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF47–49,22–25. Exact Fighter row 19 and all nested choices/resources below. Earned total-character XP threshold; admitted prior adjacent Fighter level only, never skip levels. Preserve existing bounded Fighter1->2 fixed/roll retain-Defense/mastery fixture; new options require their exact owners. Apply new feature contracts once; cumulative Champion features at/below class level; refresh Second Wind/mastery/Surge/Indomitable table capacities, not free recovery on level-up; explicit optional base Fighting Style replacement at each Fighter level. Class feature execution is independently owned. All inherited features remain gated. No unrestricted direct higher-level creation.

For each exact predicate below: deterministic positive and independently violated negative fixtures, unsupported/forged origin/level/owner rejection, inert prepare/cancel with no dice/state/history changes, explicit confirmed choice, stale revision rejection, stable action-ID replay after lost response and durable reload, concurrent confirmation applies once, atomic cost/dice/history/database rollback including injected write failures, no private DC/hidden target/lore disclosure. Shared engine through web AND trusted TUI: disabled/unavailable explanations, confirmation/cancel/reconnect/retry and keyboard/phone journeys. Injectable dice unit tests plus isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests; frontend build/changed-file lint/behavior fixtures and TUI command tests. GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./... . Feature tests use isolated entitlements; only separately qualified admission/transition may grant them. Unknown outcomes never imply success/failure. Outcome-dependent reactions such as Tactical Mind and Indomitable require a disclosed qualifying outcome. Heroic Inspiration remains available immediately after an owned known die even when the DC and outcome are undisclosed. No inference, deployment, grants, coverage or Full Rules promotion from planning. For passive/automatic source benefits, confirmation belongs to the triggering action or turn; never invent an optional activation or extra action cost.

Ownership: execution and admission are separate contracts. #427/#428 completed rests under272; #429 reusable XP/PB/CON under336 (Barbarian adapter remains D12/fixed7); Fighter D10/fixed6 separately owned here. #430 under333 provenance; #333 origins/#335 multiclass retain policy. #384 durable choices/#389 capped ability application; #385–401 exact feat effects; #487 Incapacitated/Unconscious, #488 Charmed/Frightened/Prone; #489–496 eight separate masteries under278; #58 sheet. #273 casting modes is not sheet ownership. #351–353 and #382 retain exact effect/concentration/Cleric eligibility paths; this Fighter decision grants none of their access. No generic spell implementation.

graph.title: Resolve shared Heroic Inspiration through immediate owned typed-die windows
graph.body:
<!-- edda-325:heroic-inspiration -->
Parent #50; decision #325; roadmap #47. One PR. Task Size L.

Required native path: this terminal -> #728 -> #337.

Pinned SRD5.2.1 PDF47–49 and explicitly cited consumed rules. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md. Fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF183 Heroic Inspiration; Champion grant PDF49, Human Resourceful remains #333. One shared durable PC-held boolean pool, maximum one; generic receipt/provenance with NO automatic gains. Immediately after rolling ANY owned known typed die, may expend held Heroic Inspiration to reroll that single die and MUST use new face even when worse. Not only d20, not entire dice pool, not a later arbitrary history reroll. Deterministic bounded positive/negative adapters are mandatory for current shared-engine ability-check/saving-throw d20, weapon attack d20 and individual weapon-damage d8, existing healing dice, Fighter advancement d10/fixed-choice rejection, and individually typed feat/resource dice when their exact effect owner is qualified. Each die role names its existing resolver and immediate phase; keep unsupported/unregistered adapters unavailable. Preserve original face, chosen die identity, replacement face, final dependent outcome and source provenance; one immediate window, explicit use/decline, no intervening roll/action, immutable original receipt plus final replacement reconciliation. Source gain producers remain separate: Champion751 can grant ONLY during combat at start of own turn without it; Human Resourceful is owned by333, never enabled here. If a NEW gain arrives while already held, it is lost unless explicitly given to a PC who lacks it; transfer this new gain only, no stockpiling or invented transfer of previously held inspiration, no recursive duplicate gain. Overflow transfer requires known owned/authorized PC context, never foreign/NPC/hidden actors or private roll disclosures. Stable action/roll/gain IDs bind pool cost, die replacement, dependent effects and history atomically; reload/concurrent use applies once, all injected failure paths roll back cost/dice/effect/history. Bardic Inspiration512 remains a different resource and is not reused. No species/class eligibility or spell work. All feature/admission consumers require qualified typed adapter; generic pool presence does not qualify every roll. Parent50; exact native prerequisites61/64/65. Shared qualification paths: this terminal->279 and280; this terminal->751->728->337 and directly->728->337. Positive: a known owned ability-check die with secret DC and undisclosed outcome opens the immediate Heroic Inspiration use/decline window; a worse reroll must be kept, while the DC and outcome remain undisclosed. Negative: that same unknown outcome cannot open Tactical Mind or Indomitable, and hidden/foreign dice, stale windows and unregistered adapters cannot open Heroic Inspiration.

For each exact predicate below: deterministic positive and independently violated negative fixtures, unsupported/forged origin/level/owner rejection, inert prepare/cancel with no dice/state/history changes, explicit confirmed choice, stale revision rejection, stable action-ID replay after lost response and durable reload, concurrent confirmation applies once, atomic cost/dice/history/database rollback including injected write failures, no private DC/hidden target/lore disclosure. Shared engine through web AND trusted TUI: disabled/unavailable explanations, confirmation/cancel/reconnect/retry and keyboard/phone journeys. Injectable dice unit tests plus isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests; frontend build/changed-file lint/behavior fixtures and TUI command tests. GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./... . Feature tests use isolated entitlements; only separately qualified admission/transition may grant them. Unknown outcomes never imply success/failure. Outcome-dependent reactions such as Tactical Mind and Indomitable require a disclosed qualifying outcome. Heroic Inspiration remains available immediately after an owned known die even when the DC and outcome are undisclosed. No inference, deployment, grants, coverage or Full Rules promotion from planning. For passive/automatic source benefits, confirmation belongs to the triggering action or turn; never invent an optional activation or extra action cost.

Ownership: execution and admission are separate contracts. #427/#428 completed rests under272; #429 reusable XP/PB/CON under336 (Barbarian adapter remains D12/fixed7); Fighter D10/fixed6 separately owned here. #430 under333 provenance; #333 origins/#335 multiclass retain policy. #384 durable choices/#389 capped ability application; #385–401 exact feat effects; #487 Incapacitated/Unconscious, #488 Charmed/Frightened/Prone; #489–496 eight separate masteries under278; #58 sheet. #273 casting modes is not sheet ownership. #351–353 and #382 retain exact effect/concentration/Cleric eligibility paths; this Fighter decision grants none of their access. One reviewable PR. Source: SRD5.2.1 PDF49-52 and exact named clauses below. Pin 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership boundaries are Edda additions.

Scope and source-bound positive/negative deterministic fixtures: PDF50: Bonus Action costs1 Focus for two Unarmed Strikes, no prior Attack clause. Positive two sequential confirmed strikes; negative insufficient Focus/second Bonus Action; all cost and damage atomic. Authoritative source entitlement: Monk level at least2; feature tests use isolated entitlements, not grants.

For this one PR, preview is inert; explicit confirmation revalidates authoritative eligibility, source/version, target facts and expected revision. Persist choice, exact dice, once-only cost/use and history atomically. Receipt replay/retry/reload returns the same result without rerolling or charging again. Inject history failure for full rollback; race two confirmations and require one commit; stale/foreign/unsupported state rejects without mutation. Prove this with deterministic dice and isolated PostgreSQL handler/state fixtures. Disclose only player-known targets, choices, costs and source derivations; hidden/foreign facts never enter previews, receipts or errors. Shared engine serves web and TUI: explicitly expose supported choices or show unavailable with a reason on both; require desktop/phone confirmation and reconnect plus TUI behavior fixtures before availability. No Full Rules/coverage promotion. Higher-level isolated fixture state never grants production entitlement. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p 2 ./...; changed UI requires build, focused lint and behavior tests. Prepare performs no dice rolls or writes; cancellation is inert. Confirmation atomically commits action/resource costs, dice, target/effect state, derived sheet and history with one durable receipt.

Feature execution uses isolated entitlements, never production class admission. Class applications consume implemented contracts and grant once. One reviewable PR. Source: SRD5.2.1 PDF49-52 and exact named clauses below. Pin 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership boundaries are Edda additions.

Scope and source-bound positive/negative deterministic fixtures: PDF51: one ASI feat or another qualified feat at each named Monk level; #384 validates selection, #389 applies capped ability increases; exact385-401 effect owners execute. Positive source-qualified choice; negative prerequisite/cap bypass or repeated grant. Authoritative source entitlement: Monk level at least4; feature tests use isolated entitlements, not grants.

For this one PR, preview is inert; explicit confirmation revalidates authoritative eligibility, source/version, target facts and expected revision. Persist choice, exact dice, once-only cost/use and history atomically. Receipt replay/retry/reload returns the same result without rerolling or charging again. Inject history failure for full rollback; race two confirmations and require one commit; stale/foreign/unsupported state rejects without mutation. Prove this with deterministic dice and isolated PostgreSQL handler/state fixtures. Disclose only player-known targets, choices, costs and source derivations; hidden/foreign facts never enter previews, receipts or errors. Shared engine serves web and TUI: explicitly expose supported choices or show unavailable with a reason on both; require desktop/phone confirmation and reconnect plus TUI behavior fixtures before availability. this save only once per turn.

Every target/action/numeric/condition/timing predicate needs a positive fixture and independent violation with no mutation; injectable dice and explicit trusted facts, never inference. Unknown variants remain unavailable.

Explicit isolated source entitlement only; no production admission. Own Ranger class level and selected source choices, never total character level for feature eligibility.

For this one PR, preview is inert; explicit confirmation revalidates authoritative eligibility, source/version, target facts and expected revision. Persist choice, exact dice, once-only cost/use and history atomically. Receipt replay/retry/reload returns the same result without rerolling or charging again. Inject history failure for full rollback; race two confirmations and require one commit; stale/foreign/unsupported state rejects without mutation. Prove this with deterministic dice and isolated PostgreSQL handler/state fixtures. Disclose only player-known targets, choices, costs and source derivations; hidden/foreign facts never enter previews, receipts or errors. Shared engine serves web and TUI: explicitly expose supported choices or show unavailable with a reason on both; require desktop/phone confirmation and reconnect plus TUI behavior fixtures before availability. No Full Rules/coverage promotion. Higher-level isolated fixture state never grants production entitlement. Exact licensed source; implement ONLY bounded clause above, other parts retain their separate owners:

Meld into Stone
Level 3 Transmutation (Cleric, Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: Action or Ritual
Range: Touch
Components: V, S
Duration: 8 hours
You step into a stone object or surface large enough
to fully contain your body, merging yourself and
your equipment with the stone for the duration.
You must touch the stone to do so. Nothing of your
presence remains visible or otherwise detectable by
nonmagical senses.
While merged with the stone, you can’t see what
occurs outside it, and any Wisdom (Perception)
checks you make to hear sounds outside it are made
with Disadvantage. You remain aware of the pas-
sage of time and can cast spells on yourself while
merged in the stone. You can use 5 feet of movement
to leave the stone where you entered it, which ends
the spell. You otherwise can’t move.
Minor physical damage to the stone doesn’t harm
you, but its partial destruction or a change in its
shape (to the extent that you no longer fit within it)
expels you and deals 6d6 Force damage to you. The
stone’s complete destruction (or transmutation into
a different substance) expels you and deals 50 Force
damage to you. If expelled, you move into an unoc-
cupied space closest to where you first entered and
have the Prone condition.

Direct verified spell-heading locator: PDF148. Casting ability and eligibility come from the qualified casting source; WIS is only the Ranger fixture, never a generic shared spell hardcode.

Dependency gateway expresses build/qualification coupling ONLY. It adds no runtime Spellcasting, active Concentration or active encounter requirement to ordinary leaves. Each leaf must test its own actual positive/negative owner outputs; gateway closure is insufficient. Source273 planning closure supplies no ritual/material/mode execution: this bounded spell/class adapter must implement its stated modes against qualified source eligibility, otherwise remain unavailable. Concrete current seams to inspect: internal/rules/srd521/spell.go, internal/game/spell_preview.go, internal/game/faith_effects.go, and shared durable confirmation handler. These existing narrow fixtures do not admit a broader mode.

Inherited casting source PDF104-106, exercised by this bounded spell/mode adapter, not implemented by273 planning closure: trained armor; source-prepared/access eligibility; prepared Ritual-tag spell may take normal casting time+10min with NOslot; cantrip NOslot; exact qualified freecast source charge distinct from slot; at mostONE spell-slot expenditure to cast perTURN, not a ban on free/cantrip casts. Casting1min+ takesMagicActioneachturn andConcentration; interruptedcasting fails WITHOUTslot expenditure andmustrestart. Vnormalvoice,notgagged/magicalSilence; Srequireshand; Mhandaccess maybesameasS; focusheld andsubstitutionONLYif sourceallows andmaterialUNPRICED/UNCONSUMED. Exactpriced/consumedmaterial paid once. SpellDC8+qualifiedcastingmodifier+liveTOTALPB;spellattackmodifier=qualifiedmodifier+liveTOTALPB. Clearpath excludesTotalCover unlessexplicitspell exception. Source-defined movableeffects doNOTgaininventedcast-range leash. OngoingTIMESPANspell maybedismissedNOACTIONbycaster onlywhileNOTIncapacitated;recast/expiry/otherendingsstillapply. Same-spell effects donotstack:mostpotent,mostrecentiftied;duration/sourcecontributions retained independently. Legitimate cast on unobserved invalidtargetstillspendsslot,looks likesuccessfulsave ifsuccessfulsave normallynoeffect;never revealinvalidnature. This differs from pre-confirm foreign/stale/unsupported requests rejectedwithoutmutation. Trusted facts only;unknown facts neverinferred.

Invalid-target disclosure distinction: privately known AUTHORITATIVE invalidity still permits the source-confirmed slot cast, spending the slot and applying no-effect/apparent-successful-save rules without leaking the reason. Missing, unverifiable or unauthorized facts remain unavailable; no inference and no client-supplied private-target validity. Source invalidity is distinct from stale/foreign/unsupported request rejection.

Source: English SRD5.2.1,exact PDF locators below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Exact scope and deterministic positive/negative controls:
PDF63: Rogue11 up to2 strike effects,pay EACH before rolling;6d6 minus1minus1=4d6. Reject3 effects,grant at10,free second effect.

Preview inert: no writes or dice. Explicit confirmation revalidates source,actor,campaign,revision,target,range,timing,cost and qualification. Injectable dice; atomic choice/effect/resource/history persistence. Retry/replay/reload/reconnect returns same receipt,conflicting payload rejects,concurrent confirmations commit ONCE. Inject failures for complete isolated PostgreSQL rollback. Web AND TUI expose supported choices/unavailable reasons; accessible cancel/confirm/reconnect; changed web requires desktop/phone fixtures,build and focused lint. Automatic effects belong to triggering confirmed event,not optional new activation. Unknown/private facts unavailable without leaking hidden reasons. Short tests are not integration-tag PostgreSQL/browser/device proof. No production/inference/runtime promotion. Class-total levels integer1-20,not booleans/fractions; each admitted class positive,post-transition total<=20; later-class variants require own multiclass eligibility,first-character variants do not acquire a multiclass prerequisite at runtime. Spell Recall needs actual Spellcasting; ordinary feats have no blanket casting/encounter requirement. Slot-cast one/turn applies only to slot expenditure TO CAST; authoritative confirmed invalid target spends slot/no effect with source-private filtering; unauthorized/unverifiable facts unavailable.

Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL handler/state rollback/replay/reload/concurrency fixtures are separately mandatory. Changed web: build,focused lint,desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect; trusted TUI availability/confirmation fixtures.

Ownership: each feature test uses isolated entitlements; source import,Task closure and planning277/278/273 never implement effects. Actual qualified source-bound output required before availability. Generic canonical identity/eligibility/typed-dispatch permission does NOT imply all-spell/item execution. Ordinary feat selection adds no blanket runtime Spellcasting/Concentration/encounter prerequisite. SpellRecall399 needs authoritative actual qualified Spellcasting; pureRogue,MagicInitiate386 and UMD alone do not grant it. HeroicInspiration774 differs from Bardic512. Existing rest427/428,transaction429,provenance430,conditions487/488/504/727/777/778,playerUnarmed779,Dash780/Disengage781/Dodge782 and feats385–401 keep exact scopes. No old bodies/parents/prerequisites are widened.

Native parent #1094; exact blockers: #1097, #1111, #1112, #1113, #1114.

<!-- edda-329:obscure -->
Decision #329; roadmap #47. One reviewable implementation/qualification PR; Task Size M.

Source: English SRD5.2.1,exact PDF locators below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Exact scope and deterministic positive/negative controls:
PDF63: Rogue14 cost3d6 DEX fail Blinded until END next target turn.7d6->4d6; reject CON save,early start-turn end,foreign condition removal.

Preview inert: no writes or dice. Explicit confirmation revalidates source,actor,campaign,revision,target,range,timing,cost and qualification. Injectable dice; atomic choice/effect/resource/history persistence. Retry/replay/reload/reconnect returns same receipt,conflicting payload rejects,concurrent confirmations commit ONCE. Inject failures for complete isolated PostgreSQL rollback. Web AND TUI expose supported choices/unavailable reasons; accessible cancel/confirm/reconnect; changed web requires desktop/phone fixtures,build and focused lint. Automatic effects belong to triggering confirmed event,not optional new activation. Unknown/private facts unavailable without leaking hidden reasons. Short tests are not integration-tag PostgreSQL/browser/device proof. No production/inference/runtime promotion. Class-total levels integer1-20,not booleans/fractions; each admitted class positive,post-transition total<=20; later-class variants require own multiclass eligibility,first-character variants do not acquire a multiclass prerequisite at runtime. Spell Recall needs actual Spellcasting; ordinary feats have no blanket casting/encounter requirement. Slot-cast one/turn applies only to slot expenditure TO CAST; authoritative confirmed invalid target spends slot/no effect with source-private filtering; unauthorized/unverifiable facts unavailable.

Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL handler/state rollback/replay/reload/concurrency fixtures are separately mandatory. Changed web: build,focused lint,desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect; trusted TUI availability/confirmation fixtures.

Ownership: each feature test uses isolated entitlements; source import,Task closure and planning277/278/273 never implement effects. Actual qualified source-bound output required before availability. Generic canonical identity/eligibility/typed-dispatch permission does NOT imply all-spell/item execution. Ordinary feat selection adds no blanket runtime Spellcasting/Concentration/encounter prerequisite. <!-- edda-329:climber -->
Decision #329; roadmap #47. One reviewable implementation/qualification PR; Task Size M.

Source: English SRD5.2.1,exact PDF locators below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Exact scope and deterministic positive/negative controls:
PDF64: Thief3 Climb Speed=current Speed; Speed30 ->30,Speed0->0. Reject flat30,Swim grant; dynamic modifiers retained.

Preview inert: no writes or dice. Explicit confirmation revalidates source,actor,campaign,revision,target,range,timing,cost and qualification. Injectable dice; atomic choice/effect/resource/history persistence. Retry/replay/reload/reconnect returns same receipt,conflicting payload rejects,concurrent confirmations commit ONCE. Inject failures for complete isolated PostgreSQL rollback. Web AND TUI expose supported choices/unavailable reasons; accessible cancel/confirm/reconnect; changed web requires desktop/phone fixtures,build and focused lint. Automatic effects belong to triggering confirmed event,not optional new activation. Unknown/private facts unavailable without leaking hidden reasons. Short tests are not integration-tag PostgreSQL/browser/device proof. No production/inference/runtime promotion. Class-total levels integer1-20,not booleans/fractions; each admitted class positive,post-transition total<=20; later-class variants require own multiclass eligibility,first-character variants do not acquire a multiclass prerequisite at runtime. Spell Recall needs actual Spellcasting; ordinary feats have no blanket casting/encounter requirement. Slot-cast one/turn applies only to slot expenditure TO CAST; authoritative confirmed invalid target spends slot/no effect with source-private filtering; unauthorized/unverifiable facts unavailable.

Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL handler/state rollback/replay/reload/concurrency fixtures are separately mandatory. Changed web: build,focused lint,desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect; trusted TUI availability/confirmation fixtures.

Ownership: each feature test uses isolated entitlements; source import,Task closure and planning277/278/273 never implement effects. Actual qualified source-bound output required before availability. Generic canonical identity/eligibility/typed-dispatch permission does NOT imply all-spell/item execution. Ordinary feat selection adds no blanket runtime Spellcasting/Concentration/encounter prerequisite. SpellRecall399 needs authoritative actual qualified Spellcasting; pureRogue,MagicInitiate386 and UMD alone do not grant it. HeroicInspiration774 differs from Bardic512. No old bodies/parents/prerequisites are widened.

<!-- edda-329:attunement -->
Decision #329; roadmap #47. One reviewable implementation/qualification PR; Task Size M.

Source: English SRD5.2.1,exact PDF locators below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Exact scope and deterministic positive/negative controls:
PDF64/102: Thief13 up to FOUR simultaneous,not five. Positive fourth eligible item; reject fifth,foreign/duplicate item,ignoring item-specific restrictions. No all-item activation.

Preview inert: no writes or dice. Explicit confirmation revalidates source,actor,campaign,revision,target,range,timing,cost and qualification. Injectable dice; atomic choice/effect/resource/history persistence. Retry/replay/reload/reconnect returns same receipt,conflicting payload rejects,concurrent confirmations commit ONCE. Inject failures for complete isolated PostgreSQL rollback. Web AND TUI expose supported choices/unavailable reasons; accessible cancel/confirm/reconnect; changed web requires desktop/phone fixtures,build and focused lint. Automatic effects belong to triggering confirmed event,not optional new activation. Unknown/private facts unavailable without leaking hidden reasons. Short tests are not integration-tag PostgreSQL/browser/device proof. No production/inference/runtime promotion. Class-total levels integer1-20,not booleans/fractions; each admitted class positive,post-transition total<=20; later-class variants require own multiclass eligibility,first-character variants do not acquire a multiclass prerequisite at runtime. Spell Recall needs actual Spellcasting; ordinary feats have no blanket casting/encounter requirement. Slot-cast one/turn applies only to slot expenditure TO CAST; authoritative confirmed invalid target spends slot/no effect with source-private filtering; unauthorized/unverifiable facts unavailable.

Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL handler/state rollback/replay/reload/concurrency fixtures are separately mandatory. Changed web: build,focused lint,desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect; trusted TUI availability/confirmation fixtures.

Ownership: each feature test uses isolated entitlements; source import,Task closure and planning277/278/273 never implement effects. Actual qualified source-bound output required before availability. Generic canonical identity/eligibility/typed-dispatch permission does NOT imply all-spell/item execution. Ordinary feat selection adds no blanket runtime Spellcasting/Concentration/encounter prerequisite. SpellRecall399 needs authoritative actual qualified Spellcasting; pureRogue,MagicInitiate386 and UMD alone do not grant it. HeroicInspiration774 differs from Bardic512. <!-- edda-329:scroll-light -->
Decision #329; roadmap #47. One reviewable implementation/qualification PR; Task Size M.

Source: English SRD5.2.1,exact PDF locators below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Exact scope and deterministic positive/negative controls:
PDF64/144/104-106: compose Thief scroll adapter with actual967 Light,INT; no learned/prepared/Spellcasting grant. Reject other-holder object,Huge,foreign scroll,slot spending or ritual/upcast. Own ongoing Light dismissal NO ACTION when not Incapacitated; Incapacitated alone does not end nonconcentration Light.

Preview inert: no writes or dice. Explicit confirmation revalidates source,actor,campaign,revision,target,range,timing,cost and qualification. Injectable dice; atomic choice/effect/resource/history persistence. Retry/replay/reload/reconnect returns same receipt,conflicting payload rejects,concurrent confirmations commit ONCE. Inject failures for complete isolated PostgreSQL rollback. Web AND TUI expose supported choices/unavailable reasons; accessible cancel/confirm/reconnect; changed web requires desktop/phone fixtures,build and focused lint. Automatic effects belong to triggering confirmed event,not optional new activation. Unknown/private facts unavailable without leaking hidden reasons. Short tests are not integration-tag PostgreSQL/browser/device proof. No production/inference/runtime promotion. Class-total levels integer1-20,not booleans/fractions; each admitted class positive,post-transition total<=20; later-class variants require own multiclass eligibility,first-character variants do not acquire a multiclass prerequisite at runtime. Spell Recall needs actual Spellcasting; ordinary feats have no blanket casting/encounter requirement. Slot-cast one/turn applies only to slot expenditure TO CAST; authoritative confirmed invalid target spends slot/no effect with source-private filtering; unauthorized/unverifiable facts unavailable.

Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL handler/state rollback/replay/reload/concurrency fixtures are separately mandatory. Changed web: build,focused lint,desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect; trusted TUI availability/confirmation fixtures.

Ownership: each feature test uses isolated entitlements; source import,Task closure and planning277/278/273 never implement effects. Actual qualified source-bound output required before availability. Generic canonical identity/eligibility/typed-dispatch permission does NOT imply all-spell/item execution. Ordinary feat selection adds no blanket runtime Spellcasting/Concentration/encounter prerequisite.
